task: T181 time-window hard abstain (out-of-model wrapper on T170)
approach: Parse 'time' column (HH:MM:SS string, preserved by platform per PDF p13) at inference. Force action=1 (hold) for samples whose last-tick time falls in volatile windows. Time column added to config.json feature list so platform passes it; NOT fed to LGB/NN model forward.

V1_conservative.description: Abstain first 10 min + last 10 min of each session
V1_conservative.decision: NOT recommended (large negative holdout delta; removing too many profitable trades)

V2_only_open.description: Abstain first 5 min of each session only
V2_only_open.decision: Marginal negative holdout delta (-0.27). Nearly neutral — only 1 sample per (sym, session, date) abstained. May be worth platform test as lowest-risk variant.

V3_only_close.description: Abstain last 5 min of each session only

analysis.finding: All 3 variants hurt on in-sample holdout. The T170 model's conformal band already filters low-confidence calls. The remaining active trades (even during open/close volatile periods) are net-profitable in-sample, so abstaining them costs PnL.
analysis.caveat: IN-SAMPLE evaluation: models trained on dates 0-119, tested on dates 96-119. Absolute PnL inflated. Delta vs T170 is meaningful but still biased — T170 was also trained in-sample, so both see the same data.
analysis.platform_caveat: Platform = out-of-sample future dates. T170 model may overfit to open/close signals in training -> platform open/close might be noisier -> time abstain could still help on platform.
analysis.recommendation: Do not submit V1 (too aggressive: -23.4 in-sample). V2 is nearly a no-op (only 480 samples abstained out of 442k). If submitting, V2 is lowest risk. V3 likely not worth it. SOTA T170 at +34.64 remains the best submission.

notes: All 3 zips built and sent to outputs. Predictor.py verified: time column parsed but NOT fed to LGB/NN; date not used; no cross-call state; sym-agnostic forward. config.json updated to include 'time' in feature list (156 features total, was 155).
